Island_074.terrain_character: Glacial wilderness, wind-scoured ridges, giant spruce valleys
Island_074.secondary_feature: Longhouses, turf-roof compounds, rune stones, megalithic halls
Island_074.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — huge timber frames on stone plinths, very steep snow-shedding roofs, low protected entrances, communal halls, isolated fortified farmsteads. Borrowed High Kingdom masonry appears only in elite/late structures; local builders translate it into heavier, broader forms.

Island_073.terrain_character: Snowy taiga frontier and river valleys
Island_073.secondary_feature: Raised timber houses, covered walks, watchtowers, frontier markets
Island_073.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — practical timber construction, raised foundations, compact settlements, deep eaves, enclosed yards, covered streets. Great Cold North hall traditions become smaller civic halls; Crownlands planning influence appears in market squares but remains rough and frontier-built.

Island_106.terrain_character: Broken ice coast, berg channels, exposed rocky shores
Island_106.secondary_feature: Sea forts, beacon towers, wreck-built shelters, enclosed harbors
Island_106.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — stone lower walls with timber superstructures, narrow wind-resistant profiles, heavy shutters, beacon towers and protected quays. Frost Marches carpentry is adapted for salt, ice and storms; salvaged ship timbers are culturally prestigious.

Island_081.terrain_character: Fertile central lowlands and defensible civic hills
Island_081.secondary_feature: Arcaded plazas, civic halls, gatehouses, formal bridges
Island_081.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — dressed stone, measured street grids, broad arches, courtyards, formal squares, tiled or stone-edged roofs. Neighboring regions borrow Crownlands civic forms, but Crownlands itself favors symmetry, hierarchy, public monuments and visibly planned urban growth.

Island_082.secondary_feature: Bridge-castles, monasteries, cliff stairs, vertical keeps
Island_082.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — monumental vertical stonework, narrow towers, buttressed walls, steep stairs, cliff bridges and terraced monasteries. Crownlands arches become taller and narrower here; Stone Highlands quarry craft supplies material but High Kingdom masons pursue prestige rather than bulk utility.

Island_076.terrain_character: Lake valleys, wooded hills, sheltered meadows
Island_076.secondary_feature: Inns, breweries, covered bridges, lakeside piers, clustered cottages
Island_076.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — warm timber-and-stone houses, deep porches, broad hearths, low bridges, gabled inns and dense village clusters shaped around water. Breadbasket barns influence outer farms; Timberlands framing appears in finer carpentry, but Hearthland buildings remain domestic and welcoming.

Island_084.terrain_character: Dense production forest, river cuts, logging valleys
Island_084.secondary_feature: Sawmills, log bridges, timber halls, forest watchtowers
Island_084.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — oversized timber frames, exposed structural joinery, broad roofs, elevated drying lofts, log retaining walls and functional towers. Hearthlands borrows its carpentry; Timberlands architecture itself celebrates structural timber openly rather than hiding it behind decoration.

Island_093.terrain_character: Open farmland, canals, orchard belts, gentle river plains
Island_093.secondary_feature: Granaries, mills, canal locks, barns, walled orchards
Island_093.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — broad farm compounds, long barns, mill towers, canal-facing warehouses and durable plaster/stone farmhouses. Hearthlands domestic motifs appear in villages; Grand Exchange logistics influences larger granaries, but settlement layouts remain land- and water-management first.

Island_088.terrain_character: Dense harbor district and engineered waterfront
Island_088.secondary_feature: Guild halls, cranes, customs houses, covered markets, warehouses
Island_088.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — tall narrow mercantile buildings, arcaded quays, warehouse rows, cranes, counting houses and mixed imported materials. This is the most cosmopolitan region: foreign styles are visible, but adapted to dense commerce, firebreaks, loading access and waterfront efficiency.

Island_077.terrain_character: Industrial terraces, rail cuts, workshop districts
Island_077.secondary_feature: Machine halls, gantries, utility towers, viaducts, test yards
Island_077.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — brick and stone industrial shells, long-span roofs, exposed mechanisms, service gantries, rail viaducts and modular workshop bays. Red Clay Basin brick craft is transformed into engineering architecture; Grand Exchange warehouse logic becomes highly standardized production space.

Island_089.terrain_character: Bright coastal terraces and artisan quarters
Island_089.secondary_feature: Courtyard workshops, glazed facades, dye houses, decorative arcades
Island_089.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — carved or patterned facades, colored glass, tile, concrete and plaster accents, intimate courtyards and street-facing workshops. Crownlands geometry is softened and ornamented; Grand Exchange merchant houses influence mixed shop-residence forms.

Island_075.terrain_character: Dark forest edge, misty uplands, defensive clearings
Island_075.secondary_feature: Palisaded hamlets, ward towers, fortified farmhouses, abandoned ruins
Island_075.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — compact defensive compounds, limited windows, heavy timber shutters, crooked reused masonry, ditch-and-palisade edges and watch structures. Hearthlands house forms survive here in hardened form; abandoned older layers remain incorporated rather than cleared.

Island_087.terrain_character: Wetlands, mangrove channels, unstable marsh ground
Island_087.secondary_feature: Stilt towns, boardwalks, raised storehouses, marsh shrines
Island_087.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — pile foundations, lightweight upper structures, long boardwalk spines, roofed docks, narrow boatsheds and elevated communal buildings. Sunken Coast tidal knowledge influences foundations, while local builders favor flexible timber over heavy masonry.

Island_086.terrain_character: Quarry cliffs, exposed ridges, highland terraces
Island_086.secondary_feature: Dry-stone villages, retaining walls, quarry halls, cliff roads
Island_086.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — massive low stone walls, deep-set openings, retaining terraces, stepped streets and practical quarry-built civic halls. High Kingdom borrows its masonry skill, but Stone Highlands favors durability and direct expression of geology rather than monumental display.

Island_083.secondary_feature: Brickworks, kilns, shaded courtyards, stepped mesa towns
Island_083.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — brick, terracotta and packed-earth masses, flat or shallow roofs, shaded arcades, internal courtyards and stepped construction following mesa shelves. Engineer's Reach imports its brick; local settlements emphasize thermal mass, shade and kiln-centered production.

Island_080.secondary_feature: Fishing villages, tidal warehouses, sea walls, flooded ruins
Island_080.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — stilted quays, broad decks, raised storehouses, tidal gates, seawalls and houses oriented to boat access. Blackfen pile-building and Sapphire Coast stonework both appear, but Sunken Coast settlements are shaped primarily by tide height and changing shoreline.

Island_090.terrain_character: Deep caverns, geode chambers, ancient subterranean voids
Island_090.secondary_feature: Crystal galleries, cavern bridges, carved halls, geometric ruins
Island_090.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — carved rather than built spaces, suspended bridges, precise geometric openings, monumental underground halls and controlled crystal lighting. Surface influences are sparse; newer research enclaves imitate ancient proportions without fully understanding their origin.

Island_047.terrain_character: Basalt slopes, caldera walls, lava-cut terraces
Island_047.secondary_feature: Foundries, lava channels, blackstone arches, furnace citadels
Island_047.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — thick basalt masonry, vaulted hot-work halls, open lava channels, massive buttresses, heat-separated courtyards and fortress-like industrial forms. Ember Coast borrows heavily from this tradition but makes it harsher and more portal-driven.

Island_097.terrain_character: Coves, cliffs, hidden anchorages, layered harbor slopes
Island_097.secondary_feature: Freeport docks, taverns, rope bridges, shipyards, improvised forts
Island_097.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — intentionally mixed and opportunistic: captured ship timber, reused stone, stacked warehouses, additions built over additions, narrow alleys and suspended walkways. Imported styles remain legible because the culture prizes reuse and adaptation rather than uniformity.

Island_102.terrain_character: Volcanic coast, ash fields, portal-industrial enclaves
Island_102.secondary_feature: Portal bastions, blackstone works, furnace districts, fortified causeways
Island_102.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — severe blackstone/basalt complexes, protected portal courts, narrow defensible streets, heavy arches, chimney masses and compartmentalized industrial districts. Volcano masonry is the strongest outside influence, but Nether materials push the region toward darker, more fortified forms.

Island_096.terrain_character: Coral shelf, reef channels, pale coastal terraces
Island_096.secondary_feature: Sea towers, reef gardens, water arches, guardian monuments
Island_096.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — pale stone, prismarine accents, repeated arches over water, stepped seawalls, towers aligned to channels and monumental marine complexes. Sunken Coast tidal engineering is refined into more formal civic design; underwater and shoreline spaces are treated as one continuous city.

Island_085.terrain_character: Tropical hills, fertile coasts, bamboo and orchard belts
Island_085.secondary_feature: Veranda houses, raised roofs, farm compounds, colorful waterfronts
Island_085.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — open-sided structures, deep shade, high ventilated roofs, verandas, light raised foundations and lush courtyard compounds. Sapphire Coast masonry appears in wealthier ports; Breadbasket farm organization is adapted to tropical crops and animal husbandry.

Island_095.terrain_character: Narrow passages, strategic crossings, transport corridors
Island_095.secondary_feature: Lighthouses, terminals, rail halls, bridge towers, inns
Island_095.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — infrastructure-first settlements organized around arrival and departure: long platforms, signal towers, ferry halls, bridgeheads, hostels, warehouses and navigation markers. Styles from every region appear, but standardized wayfinding and movement geometry give Transit Isles a recognizable identity.

Island_128.terrain_character: Remote fog islands, strange cliffs, concealed interior basins
Island_128.secondary_feature: Observatories, hidden compounds, impossible-looking towers, secret entrances
Island_128.lore_notes: Architecture grammar — sparse settlement footprints, strong silhouettes, secluded courtyards, concealed access routes, unusual vertical proportions and selective End-inspired materials. Imported mainland forms are deliberately abstracted so buildings feel familiar at first glance but subtly alien on approach.
